The condition gives an ellipse with foci \((\pm\sqrt5,0)\), \(a=3\), \(c=\sqrt5\), so \(b^2=9-5=4\):
\[
\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1.
\]
Optimize \(g(x,y)=2x-3y-12\) on this ellipse. At extrema,
\[
(2,-3)=\lambda\left(\frac{2x}{9},\frac y2\right),
\]
so \(y=-\frac23 x\). Substituting:
\[
\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{4x^2/9}{4}=1
\Rightarrow \frac{2x^2}{9}=1
\Rightarrow x=\pm \frac{3}{\sqrt2},\quad y=\mp \sqrt2.
\]
Then
\[
g\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt2},-\sqrt2\right)=6\sqrt2-12,
\]
\[
g\left(-\frac{3}{\sqrt2},\sqrt2\right)=-6\sqrt2-12.
\]
Both are negative, so
\[
\min f=12-6\sqrt2,\qquad \max f=12+6\sqrt2.
\]
Thus their product is
\[
(12+6\sqrt2)(12-6\sqrt2)=144-72=72.
\]
\[
\boxed{72}
\]
